verified_signals.signal: FY2025 results (published 30/04/2026) state the estate at 31/12/2025 as 1,220 ATMs and 264 MFMs (multifunction machines, i.e. machines that also take cash in) = 1,484 units; the POS acquiring estate grew 25.8% vs 2024; digital-infrastructure investment was 'aproape 235 milioane lei' (~RON 235m, c.EUR 47m) in 2025; the bank is #3 in the Romanian banking system by number of devices. Card transactions +27% by count / +25.3% by value; POS transaction volumes +49% by count and 'over 88%' by value. Group net profit RON 815.1m (+18.5%), group assets RON 107.7bn, total capital ratio 31.2%, cost/income 48.6%.
verified_signals.source_name: CEC Bank - Grupul Financiar CEC Bank: Rezultate financiare pentru anul 2025
verified_signals.implies: Only 264 of 1,484 units are deposit-capable multifunction machines - about 18% of the estate - leaving a large cash-in/recycling white space at Romania's #3 device operator; POS growth of this order supports acquiring/terminal-estate and managed-services propositions.
verified_signals.likelihood: High - modernisation is a standing multi-year programme the bank restates every year
verified_signals.followup: Name the ATM/MFM OEM and the maintenance incumbent; establish how many of the 264 MFMs are true recyclers (cash re-dispensed) vs deposit-only, since that changes the replacement case entirely.
verified_signals.verifier_note: Fetched the CEC release directly with a desktop User-Agent (HTTP 200) and read the Romanian body. Every figure is verbatim: 'La finalul anului 2025, reteaua Bancii includea 1.220 ATM-uri si 264 MFM-uri, timp in care reteaua POS a crescut cu 25,8% fata de 2024. Astfel, Banca se mentine pe locul 3 in sistemul bancar din Romania dupa numarul de echipamente'; 'valoarea acestora fiind de aproape 235 milioane de lei'; 'Numarul tranzactiilor cu carduri a crescut cu 27%, iar valoarea acestora cu 25,3%'; 'volumele de tranzactionare prin POS-uri au crescut cu 49% ca numar si cu peste 88% ca valoare'; 'Profit net de 815,1 milioane lei la nivel de Grup (+18,5%)'; 'Rata fondurilor proprii totale a ajuns la 31,2%'; 'raportul cost-venituri ... de la 49,5% la 48,6%'. Dateline 'Bucuresti, 30.04.2026' confirmed. 1,220+264=1,484 arithmetic checks. Two corrections to the researcher's wording: the POS figure is +88% or MORE ('peste 88%'), and I removed the unverified superlative 'largest cash-recycler white space in Romania' - the release supports the 264/1,484 ratio but makes no cross-bank comparison, and MFM does not necessarily mean recycler.

verified_signals.signal: The Pillar 3 / transparency report for 2025 (Pillar 3 = the disclosure report banks must publish on capital, risk and organisation), posted to cec.ro in July 2026, states that at 31/12/2025 the bank's organisational structure comprised 46 directorates/independent services and assimilated entities, 1,011 territorial units, 16 standing operational committees, and 4,893 employees (4,887 full-time equivalents plus 6 part-time).
verified_signals.source_name: CEC Bank - Raport privind cerintele de transparenta si publicare 2025 (PDF, p.3 'Structura organizatorica a CEC Bank')
verified_signals.implies: A hard denominator for branch automation: 1,011 territorial units against 1,484 machines is under 1.5 devices per unit, and management has said publicly (see the Podaru signal) that units will be converted rather than closed - implying an in-branch recycler / self-service-zone programme addressable across a four-figure site base.
verified_signals.followup: Ask for the split of the 1,011 units by format (sucursala / agentie / punct de lucru) and how many are customer-facing with a cash desk - that is the real addressable base for in-branch recyclers, and it is smaller than 1,011.
verified_signals.verifier_note: Downloaded the 181-page PDF (3.8 MB, HTTP 200) and extracted the text layer with pdfminer. Section 3 reads verbatim (report is written without diacritics): 'La data de 31.12.2025, in cadrul structurii organizatorice a Bancii functionau: - 46 de Directii, Servicii independente si entitati asimilate acestora; - 1011 unitati teritoriale; - 16 comitete operationale de lucru, permanente ... - 4893 angajati din care: 4887 salariati in echivalent norma intreaga si 6 salariati cu norma partiala.' All figures confirmed exactly. One caveat I have added to the followup: 1,011 is an ORGANISATIONAL-STRUCTURE count of territorial units, not an audited count of customer-facing physical branches, so the addressable in-branch base may be lower. It is corroborated at the order of magnitude by CEC management's own 'over 1,000 branches and territorial units' (Wall-Street.ro, 06/04/2026). I set source_date to 31/07/2026 because the researcher gave only 'Jul-2026'; the file path is dated 2026-07 and the document is the FY2025 disclosure.

verified_signals.signal: On 07/06/2026 Romania's Competition Council announced record fines totalling RON 3.73bn (c.EUR 710m) on 10 banks for coordinating conduct in the ROBOR fixing procedure (ROBOR = the Romanian interbank reference rate used to price variable-rate loans). CEC Bank's share is RON 332.98m. On 08/06/2026 CEC Bank publicly rejected the decision as 'profund nejustificata, lipsita de fundament juridic solid' and said it will contest it in court.
verified_signals.source_name: CEC Bank statement 'CEC Bank respinge cu fermitate decizia Consiliului Concurentei si va contesta sanctiunea' (primary, for the rejection and date); Competition Council communique + bankingnews.ro per-bank fine table (for the amounts)
verified_signals.implies: RON 332.98m is c.41% of FY2025 group net profit (332.98/815.1 = 40.8%). Expect provisioning pressure and tighter scrutiny of 2026-27 discretionary capex - argue opex / managed-service / as-a-service commercial models rather than capex hardware purchases.
verified_signals.likelihood: High - the provision and appeal process runs through 2026-27
verified_signals.followup: Watch for the provision in the H1-2026 interim accounts (CEC has historically posted interim IFRS statements around October) and for the published decision text on consiliulconcurentei.ro once that site is reachable.
verified_signals.verifier_note: I confirmed the CEC-side facts from the bank's own page (HTTP 200 via desktop UA): JSON-LD datePublished '06/08/2026' (= 08/06/2026) and the verbatim rejection text about the Competition Council sanctioning 'cele 10 banci din Romania care participa la procesul de fixing al pietei'. IMPORTANT: CEC's own statement contains NO monetary figure - I searched the page for '332', '3,73', 'miliarde' and 'milioane lei' and found zero hits, so the amounts do NOT rest on the primary source the researcher cited. The regulator's own communique exists at https://www.consiliulconcurentei.ro/comunicate/consiliul-concurentei-a-sanctionat-10-banci-cu-amenzi-in-valoare-de-373-miliarde-lei/ but the whole consiliulconcurentei.ro domain returns HTTP 503 behind a JavaScript browser-verification challenge to both curl-with-desktop-UA and the fetch tool, so I could not read it. I therefore verified the figures against press: bankingnews.ro publishes the full per-bank table and gives CEC Bank SA = 332,98 million lei, total 3.73bn lei / c.EUR 710m, announced 07/06/2026; the RON 3.73bn / EUR 710m total is independently corroborated by Bloomberg, Concurrences and Romania Insider. One outlier (athens-times.com) reports EUR 819m - I regard that as erroneous given three better sources agree on EUR 710m. Because the per-bank figure rests on press rather than the regulator, confidence stays Medium and must not be promoted without reading the decision itself. The researcher's '~41% of FY2025 net profit' arithmetic checks out.

verified_signals.signal: On 16/07/2026 CEC Bank launched Incasari Instant in euro - incoming instant euro credit transfers credited in seconds, available at any hour including weekends and public holidays, for both retail and corporate customers. Under the EU Instant Payments Regulation (Regulation (EU) 2024/886), payment service providers in non-euro-area Member States such as Romania must be able to RECEIVE instant euro credit transfers by 09/01/2027 and to SEND them, plus operate Verification of Payee (a check that the payee name matches the IBAN before the payer confirms), by 09/07/2027.
verified_signals.source_name: CEC Bank press release 'CEC Bank lanseaza Incasarile Instant in euro'; ECB - Instant Payments Regulation timetable
verified_signals.implies: The receive-side obligation is met roughly six months early; the send-side, Verification of Payee and the associated 24/7 real-time fraud and sanctions screening are still open and fall due 09/07/2027 - a direct, deadline-driven opening for transaction-monitoring/AML and payment-fraud tooling.
verified_signals.likelihood: Certain - it is a regulatory deadline, not a discretionary project
verified_signals.followup: Ask who supplies the instant-payments fraud/sanctions screening layer, and whether the Temenos Payments scope covers Verification of Payee or whether a third party is being sourced for it.
verified_signals.verifier_note: CEC page fetched HTTP 200; JSON-LD datePublished '07/16/2026' (= 16/07/2026) and the description confirms verbatim: 'CEC Bank isi extinde serviciile de plati digitale si lanseaza Incasarile Instant in euro ... Serviciul este disponibil la orice ora, inclusiv in weekend si in zilele de sarbatoare' for 'clientii persoane fizice si juridice' (retail and corporate). The regulatory dates - which the researcher had only asserted - I verified against the ECB's own Instant Payments Regulation page (regulator tier), which gives for non-euro-area Member States: receiving 09/01/2027, sending 09/07/2027, verification of payee 09/07/2027, equality of charges 09/01/2027. All three of the researcher's dates are correct. Bonus detail the ECB page adds and which is worth knowing: a further 09/06/2028 date applies to payments outside business hours in the national currency for non-euro-area PSPs.

verified_signals.signal: The five pilot Digital Agencies launched 05/06/2026 - Simeria (Hunedoara), Tibanesti (Iasi), Mioveni (Arges), Jurilovca (Tulcea) and Floresti (Cluj) - combine self-service equipment available 24/7 doing cash withdrawals AND cash deposits, FX exchange, payments, transfers and personal-data updates, with remote human assistance by videobanking for account opening, lending and electronic document signing. As of the product page's last update on 26/06/2026 the count is still five; the bank states the five are a pilot stage and that it will analyse results and customer feedback with a view to extending the concept to other localities 'in the period ahead', with no target number and no date given.
verified_signals.source_name: CEC Bank press release 'CEC Bank lanseaza primele Agentii Digitale' + CEC Bank 'Agentia Digitala' product page
verified_signals.implies: The functional spec - cash in plus cash out plus FX plus bill payment in one unattended lobby - is a recycler/multifunction-kiosk spec. A pilot-to-rollout decision is the single highest-value entry point at this bank for self-service hardware, cash automation, videobanking-linked eKYC and managed services.
verified_signals.likelihood: Medium-High that a rollout decision lands within 6-12 months; note the bank has committed to extension in principle but has published no number or date
verified_signals.followup: Get the pilot equipment list and vendor; time an approach to the post-pilot review with a per-site TCO for a recycler + FX kiosk + videobanking pod. Re-check the product page monthly - a sixth address appearing is the rollout trigger.
verified_signals.verifier_note: Both pages fetched HTTP 200. Press release JSON-LD datePublished '06/05/2026' (= 05/06/2026) and confirms 'primele cinci Agentii Digitale'. Locality list confirmed verbatim: 'Agentia Simeria (Hunedoara), Agentia Tibanesti (Iasi), Agentia Mioveni (Arges), Agentia Jurilovca (Tulcea) si Agentia Floresti (Cluj)' - note the correct spelling is Tibanesti with diacritics, and the researcher's county mapping is right on all five. Operations confirmed verbatim: 'retrageri si depuneri de numerar, schimburi valutare, plati, transferuri, actualizarea datelor personale ... prin intermediul echipamentelor self-service', plus 'asistenta umana la distanta prin solutii de videobanking ... de la deschiderea de conturi si accesarea de credite, pana la semnarea electronica a documentelor'. Pilot framing confirmed verbatim: 'Cele cinci Agentii Digitale reprezinta o etapa pilot a proiectului, urmand ca banca sa analizeze rezultatele si feedbackul clientilor in vederea extinderii conceptului in alte localitati din tara, in perioada urmatoare.' The '24/7' claim is NOT in the press release but IS on the product page ('echipamente self-service disponibile 24/7'), so it stands - I have re-attributed it. Product page JSON-LD dateModified '06/26/2026' (= 26/06/2026) confirms the researcher's currency check, and the page still lists exactly five addresses, which I read individually. I softened the researcher's 'no date given' slightly: the bank does say 'in perioada urmatoare' (in the period ahead), which is a soft intent, not a commitment.

verified_signals.signal: Mugur Podaru, Director of the Remote Operations Department (Directia Operatiuni la Distanta), said on 06/04/2026 that CEC Bank does not intend to close agencies - it has already started building self-service units equipped with all the necessary machines inside the bank's own premises, keeping the digital direction while changing the agency architecture, across a network of over 1,000 branches and territorial units. No conversion target, per-site equipment count or timeline was given.
verified_signals.source_name: Wall-Street.ro interview with CEC Bank management
verified_signals.implies: CEC is converting rather than shrinking its network, against the Romanian market trend. Every converted unit needs a deposit-capable machine plus a self-service zone. NOTE FOR THE ORCHESTRATOR: this is the management-statement evidence underneath the 1,011-unit and Digital Agency signals - it is the same pipeline, so do not size it a third time.
verified_signals.followup: Request a meeting with Directia Operatiuni la Distanta; ask for the 2027 unit-conversion plan, the per-site equipment spec, and whether equipment is bought or leased.
verified_signals.verifier_note: Retrieved the Wall-Street.ro article. Publication date 06/04/2026 confirmed. Speaker and exact title confirmed: Mugur Podaru, Director, Directia Operatiuni la Distanta. Quotes confirmed: 'Banca nu are de gand sa inchida agentii' and 'Am inceput deja sa construim unitati care sunt self-service si care au toate echipamentele necesare in sediul bancii'. The 'over 1,000 branches and territorial units' network descriptor is confirmed and is consistent with the 1,011 figure in the Pillar 3 report. Confirmed that no conversion target or timeline is stated. This remains press tier - it is a journalist's interview, not a bank disclosure - so confidence stays Medium. I added an explicit anti-double-counting note to 'implies' because this signal, the 1,011-unit signal and the Digital Agency signal all describe one programme and an orchestrator could otherwise book XL three times.

verified_signals.signal: [STANDING - core-banking vendor selection dated Jan 2025] CEC Bank selected Temenos on 15/01/2025 to replace retail and corporate core banking, with Tech Mahindra and SoftCentric as delivery partners and Temenos Payments covering all domestic and cross-border payments. Eighteen months on, no go-live, phase completion or migration date has been announced by the bank, Temenos, SoftCentric or Tech Mahindra. The only 2026 status statement is the FY2025 results line (30/04/2026) that the transformation 'a avansat semnificativ, atat in zona implementarii CRM, cat si a noului Core Banking System si a platformelor conexe'.
verified_signals.source_name: Temenos press release (selection) + CEC Bank FY2025 results (status)
verified_signals.implies: A core migration still in flight means channel and device integration work (ATM/MFM host interfaces, POS/acquiring, card management) is being re-specified now - the window to position ATM middleware, device-driving software and integration/managed services is before the cutover freezes the architecture.
verified_signals.likelihood: Medium - a first go-live is plausible in 2026-27 but no date has been published by any party
verified_signals.followup: Probe Temenos/SoftCentric/Tech Mahindra channels for the phasing and the planned ATM/self-service integration layer; watch Temenos quarterly results for a first CEC go-live reference, which would be the real trigger.
verified_signals.verifier_note: Temenos press release retrieved: date 15 January 2025 confirmed; delivery partners confirmed verbatim ('delivered in collaboration with Tech Mahindra and SoftCentric'); scope confirmed verbatim ('Temenos Payments will be used for all domestic and cross-border payments'); and confirmed that the release contains NO go-live date or timeline. The FY2025 status sentence is confirmed verbatim in the 30/04/2026 CEC release I read in full. I re-ran targeted searches for a CEC/Temenos go-live announcement and found none - but note this is absence of evidence, which cannot be proven exhaustively. RE-TAGGED: the researcher had is_new=true, which is wrong - the triggering event is an 18-month-old vendor selection with no announced deadline, go-live or tender within ~18 months, so under the freshness rule it is a STANDING item. I have marked the signal text accordingly and set is_new=false. It should not be presented to sales as news.

verified_signals.entity: CEC Bank / all ATM operators in Romania
verified_signals.signal: Legislative proposal B409/2026, amending Law 209/2019 on payment services, was registered at the Senate (first chamber) on 24/06/2026 with 84 deputy signatories spanning PSD (36), AUR (23), unaffiliated (7), UDMR (6), USR (3), PNL (2), POT (2) and minority/other groups. A new Art. 221^1 would oblige every payment service provider operating cash-withdrawal ATMs in Romania to let users key in a personalised withdrawal amount, for all cardholders of PSPs authorised in Romania regardless of card issuer, and expressly states that offering fast-withdrawal preset-value buttons cannot substitute for that obligation, subject to the available cash and the banknote mix in the machine. Non-compliance is added to the Art. 230 contravention list, penalised at RON 50,000-100,000. Art. III gives operators 90 DAYS from entry into force to comply. Status at 30/07/2026: registered at the Senate for debate; favourable opinions received from the Economic and Social Council (14/07/2026) and the Legislative Council (no. 679, 22/07/2026); opinions also requested from the National Bank of Romania and the Competition Council.
verified_signals.source_name: Senate of Romania - legislative file B409/2026, with the initiator's text (26b409FG.PDF)
verified_signals.implies: If adopted, every ATM in Romania - including CEC's 1,484 ATMs/MFMs - needs an application/interface change and re-certification inside a 90-day window, which is far too short for most banks to do in-house. That is a concrete, deadline-driven, market-wide ATM software and managed-services engagement, not a CEC-only one. The explicit ban on satisfying the rule with preset-value buttons means screen-flow rework, not a config toggle.
verified_signals.likelihood: Medium - very broad cross-party sponsorship and two favourable advisory opinions, but still first-chamber stage with no vote scheduled
verified_signals.followup: Track the Senate vote and whether the 90-day term in Art. III survives into the final text; prepare a market-wide ATM-application compliance offer now, since 90 days from promulgation is not enough lead time to start selling after the fact.
verified_signals.verifier_note: I opened the Senate file (HTTP 200) AND downloaded the initiator's own text at https://www.senat.ro/legis/PDF/2026/26b409FG.PDF, which the researcher had not read. Procedural facts confirmed from the file's 'Derularea procedurii legislative': registered 24-06-2026 as b409; urgency procedure requested by the initiator the same day but the file records 'Procedura de urgenta: Nu'; sent 29-06-2026 for opinion to the National Bank of Romania, the Competition Council, the Economic and Social Council and the Legislative Council; ESC opinion 4693/14.07.2026 FAVOURABLE; Legislative Council opinion 679/22.07.2026 FAVOURABLE; stage 'inregistrat la Senat pt. dezbatere'. Substance confirmed from the bill text: new Art. 221^1(1) obliges PSPs operating cash-withdrawal ATMs to provide 'posibilitatea introducerii unei sume personalizate pentru retragerea de numerar'; (2) extends it to all cardholders of PSPs authorised in Romania 'indiferent de emitentul cardului utilizat'; (4) subjects it to available cash, banknote mix and technical/security limits. Art. II confirms the RON 50,000-100,000 fine band. THREE CORRECTIONS/ADDITIONS: (a) the researcher missed Art. III, which sets a 90-DAY compliance period from entry into force - materially raising urgency and the managed-services angle, so I added it; (b) the researcher missed Art. 221^1(3), which bars preset fast-withdrawal buttons from substituting for the obligation - this forces real screen-flow work; (c) I counted the signatories exactly: 84, not '~80', and give the party split. I kept opp_size at M rather than raising it: the bill is at first-chamber stage with no vote scheduled, and inflating it on a proposal would be unsupported.

verified_signals.signal: CEC Bank runs its own open tender channel outside the public SEAP/SICAP system and publishes calls at cec.ro/achizitii, with offers filed at the head-office registry (Calea Victoriei nr.13, camera S01, sector 3, Bucharest), bids opened without bidders present, and enquiries to the Independent Procurement Service (Serviciul Independent Achizitii, tel. 021/311.11.19, sia@cec.ro). Two distinct 2026 procedures are on the page: an IT messaging (Info SMS) solution, published 25/02/2026 with offers due 13/03/2026 and an award-result communication dated 04/03/2026; and physical-security risk analyses for CEC Bank sites, published 02/04/2026 with offers due 23/04/2026, tendered in geographic lots by county zone.
verified_signals.source_name: CEC Bank - Achizitii (procurement announcements) and the two announcement detail pages
verified_signals.implies: A monitorable, low-friction route in: CEC awards by open competitive tender on its own website rather than through the national e-procurement portal, so ATM/cash-automation/security lots surface here first and are easy to miss if you only watch SICAP.
verified_signals.likelihood: High - the channel is live and reused
verified_signals.followup: Poll cec.ro/achizitii weekly; contact Serviciul Independent Achizitii (sia@cec.ro) to be registered as a qualified supplier for self-service, cash automation and security lots.
verified_signals.verifier_note: I fetched the procurement index and BOTH announcement detail pages (all HTTP 200). Confirmed: the channel exists and is CEC's own; the registry address 'Calea Victoriei nr.13, camera S01, sector 3, Bucuresti'; bid opening 'la sediul CEC BANK S.A. din Bucuresti, fara participarea ofertantilor'; and the Independent Procurement Service contact 'Serviciul Independent Achizitii ... 021/311.11.19 ... sia@cec.ro' - the researcher's sia@cec.ro is right, it just sits on the detail pages, not the index. TWO CORRECTIONS. (1) The researcher wrote that the Info SMS tender was 're-run to 23/04/2026'. That is wrong - these are two separate procedures. Info SMS: JSON-LD datePublished 25/02/2026, deadline 13.03.2026 14:00, and the page carries a 'Comunicare rezultat procedura de atribuire ... 04.03.2026.pdf', i.e. it has already been decided. The 23.04.2026 17:00 deadline belongs to the physical-security risk-analysis tender, published 02/04/2026. (2) CONTRADICTED and corrected: the researcher claimed the security tender includes 'an annex listing the bank's sites as at 31/10/2025' and called it 'a free public inventory of the bank's physical estate'. It is not. The annex is 'Anexa 6 - Lista banci site din 31 oct 2025.pdf'. I downloaded it; the PDF uses a subset font with no ToUnicode map, so I decoded the CID stream by hand and the title reads 'LISTA ACTUALIZATA A INSTITUTIILOR DE CREDIT DIN ROMANIA SI STRAINATATE FATA DE CARE CEC BANK ARE STABILITE LIMITE DE EXPUNERE', dated 31.10.2025, and the body is a list of counterparty banks (Raiffeisen, UniCredit, Alpha Bank, Erste, Deutsche Bank, Bank of China etc.) used for bid-guarantee issuer eligibility. The identically-purposed annex in the Info SMS tender is even named in full on that page: 'Lista actualizata a institutiilor de credit din Romania si strainatate fata de care CEC BANK are stabilite limite de expunere'. There is NO public site inventory here. I removed that claim from the signal and the implies field; acting on it would have wasted time. The security tender's real annexes are a county-zone distribution and standard declarations.

verified_signals.signal: [STANDING - dated 2020-2023] The ATM/MFM OEM has never been disclosed. The multi-year replacement programme was announced 21/07/2020 (EUR 2.6m budgeted for 2020, first phase 200 ATMs by end-2020, then the whole fleet); CEC said only that the equipment is made by 'one of the largest producers globally' and that the supplier was chosen by a competitive procurement procedure in which 'the main national distributors of such equipment' took part. By 17/05/2023 approximately 1,100 units had been replaced, over 80% of the network, with large touchscreens and contactless, and all NEW equipment reading barcode/QR codes. MFMs accept cash deposits in lei and euro, do FX exchange and take bill payments in cash and by card. Separately, an integrated system for MONITORING AND MAINTENANCE of the bank's ATM and POS fleet was delivered on the Aurachain low-code platform under a partnership announced 25/02/2021, alongside SME online onboarding and online trade finance.
verified_signals.source_name: CEC Bank press releases 21/07/2020 and 17/05/2023 + Aurachain announcement 25/02/2021
verified_signals.implies: Two things for Printec: (a) the hardware incumbent is deliberately unnamed but was won through open competitive tender via national distributors - so it is contestable at the next refresh cycle rather than locked in; (b) fleet monitoring/maintenance orchestration sits on a low-code platform (Aurachain) rather than an OEM fleet-management product, so a managed-services pitch should propose integrating with that layer, not replacing it.
verified_signals.likelihood: Medium - a next refresh wave is a reasonable inference as the 2020-23 units age out from about 2027, but no refresh tender has been announced
verified_signals.followup: Identify the OEM/distributor from field photos of a CEC machine or from the 2020 tender award; check whether the Aurachain fleet-monitoring app survived the Temenos programme, since a Temenos-era replacement of it would reopen the fleet-management layer.
verified_signals.verifier_note: I read BOTH CEC press releases in full (HTTP 200 each). The 17/05/2023 release confirms: 'CEC Bank a inlocuit aproximativ 1.100 de bancomate si aparate multifunctionale vechi', 'peste 80% din intreaga retea', #3 in Romania by ATM/MFM count, touchscreens and contactless. The 21/07/2020 release (JSON-LD description dated 21.07.2020) confirms verbatim: 'Valoarea investitiilor programate pentru 2020 se ridica la 2,6 milioane de euro'; 'Pana la sfarsitul lui 2020, in prima faza a programului, vor fi inlocuite 200 de ATM-uri'; 'Echipamentele achizitionate in cadrul acestui program sunt realizate de unul dintre cei mai mari producatori la nivel global'; 'Furnizorul echipamentelor a fost ales printr-o procedura de achizitii competitiva la care au participat principalii distribuitori de astfel de echipamente la nivel national'; and the MFM capability list 'depuneri de numerar in lei si euro, operatiuni de schimb valutar si plata facturilor in numerar si cu cardul'. All confirmed - the OEM is genuinely never named. TWO CORRECTIONS. (1) The researcher wrote that the 2023 units were 'all with touchscreens, contactless and barcode/QR readers'. The release says over 80% of the NETWORK has touchscreens and contactless, and separately that 'Toate echipamentele noi permit citirea codurilor de bare/QR' - i.e. all NEW equipment reads barcode/QR, not the whole estate. Corrected in the signal text. (2) The researcher asserted the fleet-monitoring system was 'built IN-HOUSE' by the bank on Aurachain. I checked the Aurachain primary source (aurachain.ch now 301-redirects to aurachain.com): dated 25/02/2021, it confirms the three use cases including 'implementation of an integrated system for monitoring and maintenance of the bank's ATM and POS fleet', but it does NOT say who built it - the build ownership is not disclosed. I removed 'in-house' from both the signal and the implies, since the researcher's tactical conclusion rested on it. Also RE-TAGGED as [STANDING - dated 2020-2023]: the newest event here is 3+ years old and the '2027 refresh' is an inference with no announced tender, so this must not be presented as new. is_new=false retained.
